## Candidate States

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document.

```{r}
library(readxl)
library(dplyr)

df <- read_excel("carnes_legislators.xlsx")

View(df)

df %>%
  filter(!is.na(YearBorn)) %>%
  group_by(StateAbbrev) %>%
  summarise(n_legislators = n())

#making state_counts own data frame
state_counts <- df %>%
  filter(!is.na(YearBorn)) %>%
  count(StateAbbrev, name = "n_legislators")

#saving as csv
write.csv(state_counts, "state_counts.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

Work in Public Safety

-SAFTY

```{r}

library(dplyr)

public_safety_table <- df %>%
  filter(SAFTY == 1) %>%
  group_by(StateAbbrev) %>%
  summarise(
    n_public_safety = n(),
    safety_details = paste(
      paste(JobTitle, JobOrgName, sep = " — "),
      collapse = "; "
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(StateAbbrev)


public_safety_table_total <- public_safety_table %>%
  bind_rows(
    summarise(
      public_safety_table,
      StateAbbrev = "Total",
      n_public_safety = sum(n_public_safety, na.rm = TRUE),
      safety_details = NA_character_
    )
  )

public_safety_table_total
```
